artiest/yehudi-menuhin.text:
Yehudi Menuhin was born in New York in 1916 to Jewish parents and grew into one of the greatest violinists of the twentieth century. He began violin lessons at the age of four. At eight he played as a soloist with the San Francisco Symphony, and at twelve he scored a great success in Dresden and Berlin with the concertos of Bach, Beethoven and Brahms. He studied with Louis Persinger, George Enescu and Adolf Busch. In 1932 he recorded Edward Elgar's Violin Concerto with the composer himself conducting.

After the war he played with Benjamin Britten for survivors of the concentration camps, including at Bergen-Belsen. In 1947 he became the first Jewish musician to return to Germany, for concerts with Wilhelm Furtwängler. He had Bartók write a sonata for solo violin, and with the sitar player Ravi Shankar he recorded West Meets East. He also played jazz with Stéphane Grappelli. His recording contract with EMI lasted almost seventy years, from 1929 to 1999. Later he also became a conductor and founded, among other things, the Menuhin Festival Gstaad, the Yehudi Menuhin School in Surrey and an international violin competition for young talents.

Menuhin played with a warm, singing tone, and he showed that a classical musician can let other worlds inspire him. His collaboration with Shankar introduced Indian music to a large Western audience, and the duo with Grappelli proved that classical music and jazz enrich each other. In this way he belongs among the musicians who opened up the boundaries between musical cultures, long before the term world music existed.
artiest/yehudi-menuhin.listen: Listen to West Meets East and notice how Menuhin's violin and Shankar's sitar answer each other. Try to hear where the sitar stretches the melody and where the violin, by contrast, stays calmer.

artiest/yellow-magic-orchestra.text:
Yellow Magic Orchestra, YMO for short, was a Japanese electronic band from Tokyo. Haruomi Hosono (bass, keyboards, vocals), Yukihiro Takahashi (drums, vocals) and Ryuichi Sakamoto (keyboards) founded the group in 1978. All three already had experience in the music world. Hosono came from the band Happy End, Takahashi from the Sadistic Mika Band, and Sakamoto experimented with synthesizers as a student. The programmer Hideki Matsutake, who had previously worked for Isao Tomita, was regarded as a fourth member. Hosono conceived an instrumental disco band that could succeed outside Japan.

The self-titled debut was released in 1978. It included Firecracker, which became a success in the United States and Europe as Computer Game. The second album, Solid State Survivor (1979), won an award for best album in Japan and contained Behind the Mask and a mechanical version of The Beatles' Day Tripper. X∞Multiplies (1980), BGM (1981), Technodelic (1981), Naughty Boys (1983) and Service (1983) followed. After a break in 1984, Technodon appeared in 1993. In 1980 YMO was the most popular band in Japan.

The sound consisted of synthesizers, samplers, sequencers, drum machines and digital recording, blended with funk, disco, Japanese folk music and video game sounds. The lyrics were mostly in English and often science-fictional. In this way YMO applied a Western instrument in a distinctly Asian manner. In Japan the group set technopop in motion, and it is regarded as a pioneer of synth-pop, electro and techno. Even young hip hop in the Bronx took notice: Afrika Bambaataa used Firecracker in his Death Mix.
artiest/yellow-magic-orchestra.listen: Listen to Computer Game, the adaptation of Firecracker. Notice the tinny, game-like synthesizer sounds and how tight and mechanical the rhythm is.

artiest/yellowman.text:
Yellowman, born Winston Foster in 1956, is a Jamaican reggae and dancehall deejay. He grew up in a children's home and later at the Alpha Boys School in Kingston, a school with a famous musical tradition. Because he is albino, he was shunned in Jamaica. In 1978 he came second in the Tastee Talent Contest, and the following year he won it. That marked the start of his professional career. He performed often at sound system dances, especially with Aces International, and worked in the early 1980s with the producer Henry Junjo Lawes. In 1981 he became the first dancehall artist to sign with a major American label, Columbia.

His first album, Mister Yellowman, was released in 1982. Zungguzungguguzungguzeng followed in 1983 and was an immediate success. In the early 1980s he had more than forty singles and released up to five albums a year. In 1987 his version of Blueberry Hill topped the chart in Jamaica for several weeks. His sexually charged lyrics drew criticism, but he said he was simply telling what goes on behind closed doors. With the 1994 album Prayer he turned to religious themes.

Deejays talk or rap in a rhythmic style over an instrumental bass line, the riddim. Yellowman was one of the first of the new generation of dancehall deejays and brought the genre to an international audience. He was nominated for a Grammy twice.
artiest/yellowman.listen: Listen to Zungguzungguguzungguzeng and notice the nonsense words in the title and the chorus. Notice how his voice itself sets down a rhythm, almost like an extra instrument.

artiest/yes.text:
Yes is an English progressive rock band that was formed in London in 1968. The singer Jon Anderson and the bassist Chris Squire found each other through their love of harmony singing and wrote their first song together. The guitarist Peter Banks, the drummer Bill Bruford and the keyboard player Tony Kaye completed the line-up. On the first two albums, Yes (1969) and Time and a Word (1970), they played a mix of original songs and covers from rock, pop, blues and jazz.

After Steve Howe became the guitarist in 1970, the band changed course. The result was a series of albums that are regarded as classics of progressive rock: The Yes Album and Fragile in 1971, with the hit Roundabout, and Close to the Edge in 1972. Rick Wakeman joined on keyboards. Tales from Topographic Oceans followed in 1973. The group was also known for elaborate stage shows and for the sleeves by Roger Dean. In 1983 a new line-up with Trevor Rabin took on a pop-rock sound and made the album 90125, with the hit Owner of a Lonely Heart.

Yes plays long, layered pieces with complex rhythms, high, clear vocals, virtuoso guitar and keyboard playing and a melodic bass guitar. The band is regarded as one of the pioneers of progressive rock, and with changing line-ups it remained active well into the twenty-first century.
artiest/yes.listen: Listen to Close to the Edge and notice how the piece is made up of several sections, with calm and stormy passages. Try to hear how the instruments take turns, rather than playing a fixed accompaniment.

artiest/yo-yo-ma.text:
Yo-Yo Ma is an American cellist, born in Paris in 1955 to Chinese parents. His father, a violinist and composer, gave him his first cello lessons at the age of four. When he was seven the family moved to Boston and later to New York. He played for President Kennedy, appeared on American television at the age of eight under the direction of Leonard Bernstein, and studied at the Juilliard School. He then took a degree in anthropology at Harvard. He became world famous as a soloist with major orchestras.

Ma has recorded more than ninety albums and won twenty Grammy Awards. His best-known recordings are Bach's six solo suites for cello. On his instrument, a 1712 Stradivarius that once belonged to Jacqueline du Pré, he plays with a smooth, warm tone and a great deal of lyricism. For films he played on the scores of Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon (2000), Seven Years in Tibet and Memoirs of a Geisha. He also worked with Ennio Morricone.

Ma is called an omnivore, because he has also recorded Argentine tango by Astor Piazzolla, Brazilian music, bluegrass and Chinese melodies. He has made music with Bobby McFerrin, Carlos Santana, Sting, James Taylor and Miley Cyrus. He founded the Silk Road Ensemble, a collective of musicians from countries along the ancient Silk Road. In this way he shows that a classical soloist can build a bridge between cultures and genres.
artiest/yo-yo-ma.listen: Listen to his recording of the Sarabande from Bach's fifth solo suite, or to his cello in While My Guitar Gently Weeps with Carlos Santana. Notice the warm tone and how the cello almost sings.

artiest/yoasobi.text:
Yoasobi is a Japanese duo formed in 2019. Ayase writes and produces the music, and Ikura sings. The name means nightlife, and Ayase chose it because he wanted to compare his own work with Ikura's as the night, set beside the day of their separate careers. Their motto is that they turn novels into music: the songs are based on stories posted on the writing platform Monogatary.com, and later also on books, letters and other sources.

The breakthrough came in 2020 with Yoru ni Kakeru, their debut single, which spent six weeks at number one on the Billboard Japan Hot 100. It was the first song without a physical release to end the year at number one. Gunjō followed, as did Kaibutsu for the anime Beastars and Idol, the opening theme of the anime Oshi no Ko, from 2023. Idol spent 22 non-consecutive weeks at the top of the Japanese chart and became one of the best-selling songs of the year worldwide. The EPs The Book and The Book 2 were released in 2021 and The Book 3 in 2023. The duo also released English-language versions.

The music has a fast tempo and a complex structure and is described as a blend of J-pop and Vocaloid. Several magazines call Yoasobi a representative of the J-pop of the 2020s. The group shows how stories, anime and the internet together can make a new kind of pop star.
artiest/yoasobi.listen: Listen to Idol and notice the fast tempo and the rapid changes within the song. Notice how the vocals are often clear and lightning-fast at the same time, without sounding breathless.

artiest/yoko-kanno.text: Yoko Kanno (born 1963) began as a composer of video game music and played keyboards in a pop band. In anime she became known for her enormous stylistic range. For Macross Plus (1994) she wrote orchestral music, pop songs and electronic tracks side by side. For the series Cowboy Bebop (1998) she founded the band The Seatbelts, which played jazz, blues, funk and country. The opening theme Tank! is a big band number with brass, bongos and a walking bass. In Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex (2002) she combined electronics with the voice of the Russian singer Origa. Kanno shows that an anime score is more an album than a string of cues.
artiest/yoko-kanno.listen: In Tank!, listen for the brass section, the fast walking bass and the breaks in which the band briefly falls silent.

artiest/yoko-ono.text:
Yoko Ono was born in Tokyo in 1933, the daughter of a wealthy banker and former concert pianist. In 1952 she moved to New York. There, in the early 1960s, she became involved with the downtown artists, among them the Fluxus group. In 1965 she performed Cut Piece at Carnegie Recital Hall. She made performance art, films and conceptual works such as Hammer a Nail, a piece in which visitors were invited to hammer a nail into a white-painted board.

In 1966 she met John Lennon, who admired her work. They married in 1969. They used their honeymoon for a bed-in, a public protest against the war in Vietnam. Together they recorded as the Plastic Ono Band. In the 1970s Ono made experimental albums, including Yoko Ono/Plastic Ono Band in 1970, and in 1980, with Double Fantasy, made together with Lennon, she won a major prize: the album won a Grammy for Album of the Year. Lennon was murdered three weeks after its release. She later had twelve number one hits on the American dance club charts.

Ono's voice and art were long seen as difficult. She brought shrill, free vocals into pop music, and later groups such as the B-52's and Sonic Youth have named her as an example. In the Beatles story of School of Rock she appears as Lennon's new partner who sat in the studio every day, something the other Beatles were not used to. Afterwards she devoted herself to peace, including with the Imagine Peace Tower in Iceland.
artiest/yoko-ono.listen: Listen to Yoko Ono/Plastic Ono Band from 1970 and pick a track. Notice how her voice is used as an instrument, with wails and sounds instead of ordinary vocal melodies.

artiest/yoko-shimomura.text: Yoko Shimomura (born 1967) studied piano at the Osaka College of Music. In 1988 she joined Capcom, where she wrote the music for Street Fighter II (1991), with short, energetic themes for each character. The best known of these is Guile's theme. In 1993 she moved to Square and worked on Super Mario RPG (1996). With Kingdom Hearts (2002) she wrote the music for a blend of Disney and Final Fantasy. The opening piece Dearly Beloved is a short, calm piano melody. For Xenoblade Chronicles (2010) she collaborated with other composers. Her style is melodic, often with a melancholy undertone.
artiest/yoko-shimomura.listen: Notice the short, catchy melody that keeps repeating, and how a piano or synthesizer builds on it with small variations.

artiest/yosuke-yamashita.text: The pianist Yosuke Yamashita was born in Tokyo in 1942. In 1969 he formed a bassless trio that played free jazz, with the saxophonist Seiichi Nakamura and the drummer Takeo Moriyama; in the early 1970s the alto saxophonist Akira Sakata joined. Yamashita plays with great energy and hammers out fast, hard chords, often compared with the playing of Cecil Taylor. In 1974 the trio made its first European tour and played at the festival in Moers, Germany; that recording was released as Clay. Chiasma was recorded live in 1975 at the Jazztage in Heidelberg. The trio lasted until 1983. Later Yamashita wrote piano concertos, which he played under the direction of the conductor Yutaka Sado.
artiest/yosuke-yamashita.listen: Hear how the piano is played almost like a percussion instrument.

artiest/yothu-yindi.text:
Yothu Yindi is an Australian group with Aboriginal and non-Aboriginal members, formed in 1986 from two bands from 1985: the rock group Swamp Jockeys and a Yolngu folk group from the Gove Peninsula in Arnhem Land, with among others Mandawuy Yunupingu, Witiyana Marika and Gurrumul Yunupingu. In Yolngu the name means child and mother. The group combines traditional Aboriginal songs with pop and rock. Besides guitars and drums it uses the yidaki, a didgeridoo, and bilma, clapsticks made of ironwood, and traditional dance is part of the performances.

The debut album Homeland Movement was released in 1989 and had little success. The breakthrough came with Treaty, from 1991. In 1988 Prime Minister Bob Hawke had promised at the Barunga Festival that there would be a treaty with the original inhabitants. Mandawuy and his brother Galarrwuy wanted a song about the lack of progress. A dance remix by Filthy Lucre took the song to number eleven in the Australian chart, and the album Tribal Voice reached number four. The song contains both English and Yolngu lyrics. In 1990 the group founded the Yothu Yindi Foundation, which later organised the Garma Festival.

Mandawuy Yunupingu was named Australian of the Year in 1993. In 2012 the group was inducted into the ARIA Hall of Fame. Treaty brought the Aboriginal struggle for recognition into the international pop world.
artiest/yothu-yindi.listen: Listen to Treaty and notice how English and Yolngu alternate and which traditional sounds can be heard between the guitars and drums. Can you hear the yidaki?

artiest/young-disciples.text:
Young Disciples was a British-American acid jazz group, founded in London in 1990 by the singer and keyboard player Carleen Anderson, the bassist and guitarist Marco Nelson and the percussionist Femi Williams. Anderson came from the United States and had moved to London with her young son, where she met Nelson. The group signed to Talkin' Loud Records and first released Get Yourself Together.

The breakthrough came in 1991 with Apparently Nothin', which reached number thirteen in the British charts. The album Road to Freedom was released in 1991 and reached number twenty-one. It was recorded in Paul Weller's private studio, with guests such as Fred Wesley and Maceo Parker, the horn players from the funk world, and Mick Talbot and Paul Weller himself. In 1992 the group contributed a remix of Apparently Nothin' to the benefit album Red Hot + Dance. That same year Anderson left to go solo, and with that the group broke up.

Young Disciples belonged to the emerging acid jazz scene, which mixed jazz, soul and funk with hip hop rhythms. The group also had ties to British hip hop, and rappers such as MC Mell'O' and Masta Ace worked with them. The song Apparently Nothin' is regarded as one of the best-known records of that movement.
artiest/young-disciples.listen: Listen to Apparently Nothin' and notice Carleen Anderson's warm voice and the rhythmic loop beneath her singing. Can you hear the blend of jazz, soul and hip hop?

artiest/young-jeezy.text:
Jay Jenkins, known as Young Jeezy and later as Jeezy, was born in 1977 in Columbia, South Carolina, and grew up in Georgia. He began making records in 2001 under the name Lil J and first released two independent albums, Thuggin' Under the Influence in 2001 and Come Shop wit Me in 2003. In 2004 he signed with Bad Boy Records and became a member of the group Boyz n da Hood. He founded his label CTE World in 1998, at first under a different name. Later he signed with Def Jam.

His Def Jam debut, Let's Get It: Thug Motivation 101, was released in July 2005 and reached number two on the Billboard 200. From the album came Soul Survivor with Akon, which reached number four on the Billboard Hot 100 and is so far his highest chart position. The Inspiration from 2006 and The Recession from 2008 both topped the album chart. From The Recession, Put On, with Kanye West, was nominated for a Grammy. He was also heard as a guest, including on Usher's Love in This Club.

Together with T.I. and Gucci Mane, Jeezy is counted among those who brought trap, a hip hop style from Georgia with heavy bass and blaring synthesizers, to a wide audience. He emphasised street credibility and motivational lyrics about rising up, and his voice, low and hoarse, became a trademark.
artiest/young-jeezy.listen: Listen to Soul Survivor and notice the difference between his low, raw rapping in the verses and Akon's smooth singing in the chorus. What does that contrast do for the song?

artiest/youngkio.text:
YoungKio is the artist name of Kiowa Roukema, a Dutch producer and songwriter, born in 1999 and of Surinamese descent. He began making beats in 2016 in the program FL Studio, which a friend had given him as a present. His role models were producers such as Wheezy and TM88. He put his type beats on YouTube and leased them online for thirty dollars each. With the money he bought a one-year membership on the BeatStars platform.

In 2018 the American rapper Lil Nas X leased one of his beats for the song Old Town Road. The beat used a sample of Ghost IV, track 34, a composition by Nine Inch Nails from 2008. The song was released on 3 December 2018 and became a hit via the app TikTok. In 2019 it grew into one of the best-known records of the year, partly thanks to the remixes with, among others, Billy Ray Cyrus. For his work on it YoungKio received Grammy nominations.

He then signed with Victor Victor Worldwide, Universal Music Publishing Group and CashMoneyAP's production collective Cash Gang. He made beats for artists such as Lil Pump, Rico Nasty, Octavian and Skepta and Megan Thee Stallion. YoungKio stands for a new way of making records: a teenager behind his laptop who leases a beat online and can thereby produce a worldwide hit. In this way he belongs to the School of Rock story about music from cassette to cloud.
artiest/youngkio.listen: Listen to Old Town Road by Lil Nas X. Notice the slow, dark beat and the banjo, and ask yourself how a beat leased online for thirty dollars could carry such a big song.

artiest/yu-zhenfei.text:
Yu Zhenfei was a Chinese opera singer and actor who became known in the twentieth century in the genres kunqu and jingju, Peking opera. Kunqu is one of the oldest forms of traditional Chinese musical theatre. Many pieces from the classical repertoire, such as the play The Peony Pavilion from 1598, were written for this art form. It is a theatre in which singing, gesture, dance and a soft, melodious orchestra come together, in a slower and more lyrical style than Peking opera.

Yu Zhenfei was regarded as one of the leading performers of his time. In Shanghai he often appeared with the singer Yan Huizhu, the Queen of Peking Opera. Together they performed an adapted version of Qiangtou mashang. In 1960 they married. The marriage ended in tragedy in 1966: during the Cultural Revolution their house was ransacked by the Red Guards and Yan Huizhu was denounced. On the night of 10 September 1966 she took her own life, while Yu Zhenfei was in the same room.

The story of Yu Zhenfei shows how strongly traditional music and theatre were affected by the politics of that time. Opera performers were seen as representatives of an old culture, and many were persecuted. For anyone who wants to follow the musical story of China, he belongs among the musicians who kept centuries-old art forms alive.
artiest/yu-zhenfei.listen: Listen to a recording of kunqu and notice the soft, melodious orchestra and the long, sustained vocal phrases. Try to hear how unhurried the tempo is compared with Peking opera.

artiest/yung-joc.text:
Yung Joc is the stage name of Jasiel Amon Robinson, a rapper from Atlanta, born in 1980. His father had a business in hair care products and helped him get the chance to write a jingle for Revlon. He then started his own label, Mastermind, to release his music. In 2005 he met the Atlanta producer Nitti Beatz, with whom he recorded the hit It's Goin' Down in the spring. Through Russell Block Spencer of Block Entertainment he came to Bad Boy South, the label of Sean Combs.

It's Goin' Down reached number 3 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2006 and appeared on his debut album New Joc City. That also included I Know U See It. His second album Hustlenomics followed in 2007, with, among others, Coffee Shop and Bottle Poppin'. Both records reached number 3 on the Billboard 200. He was also heard as a guest rapper: on T-Pain's Buy U a Drank (Shawty Snappin'), which became number 1 in 2007, on Danity Kane's Show Stopper and on tracks by David Banner and Bobby V.

Yung Joc is one of the Atlanta rappers who brought Southern hip hop to the general public in the mid-2000s. His style is loose and melodic, with laid-back, danceable beats and a sing-song delivery that suits guest appearances on pop records well. After a lawsuit over royalties he founded his own label in 2008, Swagg Team Entertainment. Later he also became known as a television personality in the series Love & Hip Hop: Atlanta.
artiest/yung-joc.listen: Listen to T-Pain's Buy U a Drank (Shawty Snappin') and notice how Yung Joc, as a guest, complements T-Pain's vocal melody with a short, laid-back rap.

artiest/yutaka-sado.text:
Yutaka Sado is a Japanese conductor, born in 1961 in Kyoto. As a schoolboy he already earned a place at the Kansai Nikikai, a Japanese opera training programme, where he got to know the operatic repertoire with the New Japan Philharmonic and the Kyoto Symphony Orchestra. In 1987 he went to the Tanglewood Music Festival in the United States to take lessons from Seiji Ozawa. Later he also studied with Charles Dutoit and Gennady Rozhdestvensky, and with Leonard Bernstein, with whom he toured the Soviet Union and Germany.

In 1989 he won first prize at the International Competition for Young Conductors in Besançon, as the third Japanese winner after Ozawa and Yoko Matsuo. In 1995 he won the first Leonard Bernstein Jerusalem International Music Competition. From 1993 to 2011 he was principal conductor of the Orchestre Lamoureux in Paris, with which he recorded for Erato, among others. In Japan he became artistic director of the Hyogo Performing Arts Center and head of the orchestra he helped found there in 2005. He also led the Siena Wind Orchestra. From 2015 to 2025 he was principal conductor of the Tonkünstler Orchestra in Austria. In 2011 he conducted Beethoven's Ninth Symphony with ten thousand Japanese participants, in memory of the victims of the earthquake.

Sado stands in the tradition of Bernstein and Ozawa: conductors who brought classical music to a wide audience. His work shows how deeply Western orchestral culture is rooted in Japan and how Japanese conductors, since the second half of the twentieth century, have gained a permanent place on the great stages of Europe.
artiest/yutaka-sado.listen: Listen to a recording of Beethoven's Ninth Symphony and notice the final chorus, where the orchestra and a large group of singers come together. Try to hear how the conductor drives up the tempo towards the end.

artiest/yuzo-koshiro.text:
Yuzo Koshiro was born in 1967 in Hino, near Tokyo. His mother was a pianist and taught him to play at the age of three. In 1975 he took lessons for three years from Joe Hisaishi, after which he taught himself. In secondary school he began making music on the NEC PC-8801 computer, including imitations of game music by Namco, Konami and Sega. He received his first commission in 1986, at the age of eighteen, from Nihon Falcom. For that company he wrote, among other things, the music for Sorcerian and the first Ys games.

Afterwards he worked as a freelancer. For Sega he made The Revenge of Shinobi in 1989, with house and techno-like music mixed with traditional Japanese sounds. ActRaiser from 1990, by contrast, had a classical, orchestral sound. In 1990 he founded the company Ancient with his mother and his sister Ayano. He made his music for the Streets of Rage series, between 1991 and 1994, with outdated PC-8801 equipment and a programming language of his own. Critics call those soundtracks revolutionary and far ahead of their time.

Koshiro wrote music in genres such as rock, jazz, symphonic, house, electro, techno and trance. He is regarded as one of the most important innovators of chiptune and of game music, and he showed that the limited sound chips of the 1990s could produce dance-floor sound.
artiest/yuzo-koshiro.listen: Listen to Go Straight and notice the driving bass line and the drums, which make the track sound like a club record. Try to hear which sounds come from a chip and which are more like real instruments.

artiest/yvonne-loriod.text:
Yvonne Loriod was a French pianist and teacher, born in 1924 in Houilles near Paris. As a child she received piano lessons from her godmother and gave recitals at a young age, with a large repertoire of Bach, Beethoven, Chopin and Mozart. Between 1941 and 1948 she studied at the Paris Conservatoire, with Lazare Lévy and Marcel Ciampi, among others. She became one of the first pupils of Olivier Messiaen, who noticed her virtuosity and memory at once. In 1945 she gave the French premiere of Béla Bartók's Second Piano Concerto, which she had learned in eight days.

From the 1940s onwards Messiaen wrote his piano works for her, including Visions de l'Amen and Vingt Regards sur l'enfant Jésus. He said he could allow himself the greatest extravagances, because Loriod would master them anyway. Together with her sister Jeanne, who played the Ondes Martenot, she was a soloist in the Turangalîla-Symphonie. Among other things she recorded Catalogue d'oiseaux (1971). In 1961 she married Messiaen. From 1967 to 1989 she taught at the Paris Conservatoire. After his death in 1992 she completed his Traité de rythme, de couleur et d'ornithologie. She also composed herself, including Mélopées africaines.

Loriod is regarded as the most important interpreter of Messiaen's piano music. That is far more than performing: a composer wrote his music around a player, and her technique helped determine how that music sounded. As a teacher she and Messiaen passed on their knowledge to Pierre-Laurent Aimard, who still champions their work. She died in 2010.
artiest/yvonne-loriod.listen: Listen to a movement from Catalogue d'oiseaux or Vingt Regards sur l'enfant Jésus. Notice the fast, bright chords and birdlike motifs, and how far the pianist ranges across the keyboard.

artiest/zachary-levi.text:
Zachary Levi is an American actor, born in 1980 in Lake Charles, Louisiana, and raised in Ventura, California. He was on stage at the age of six in regional productions of musicals such as Grease, Oklahoma! and Oliver!. His television breakthrough came with the comedy Less Than Perfect (2002 to 2006) and above all with the action series Chuck (2007 to 2012). Later he played Fandral in the Thor films and the title role in the superhero film Shazam! (2019) and its sequel in 2023. For his role in the 2016 Broadway revival of the musical She Loves Me he was nominated for a Tony Award.

He also made himself heard in music. In the Disney film Tangled (2010) he voiced and sang the role of Flynn Rider. With Mandy Moore he sang I See the Light, a song that won a Grammy Award for Best Song Written for Visual Media. They also performed it at the Academy Awards, where it was nominated. He also sang I've Got a Dream on the soundtrack and recorded the duet Terrified with Katharine McPhee. He also took part in Band from TV, a band of actors.

Levi thus belongs among the actors who gained a place in popular music through film and musical theatre. His voice suits the kind of Disney songs that became popular again with a wide audience in the 2010s. In this way he shows how closely film and pop music are intertwined in modern entertainment culture.
artiest/zachary-levi.listen: Listen to I See the Light from Tangled and notice how Levi's voice and Mandy Moore's blend. Notice, too, how the accompaniment builds gently from soft to full.

artiest/zack-hemsey.text:
Zack Hemsey was born in 1983, grew up in New Jersey and studied music and philosophy at Rutgers University. He began as a composer and one of the five lyricists of the little-known hip hop group Nine Leaves. In 2010 he began his solo career with the album Empty Room, and since then he has released his music independently. Later came, among others, The Way in 2011, Ronin in 2013, Nomad in 2016 and Goliath in 2018, a soundtrack to a film that does not exist.

His music combines elements of alternative hip hop, alternative rock, classical orchestra and world music instruments. He became known mainly through films and trailers. Mind Heist from 2010 is heard in the trailer for Inception and in the game Madden NFL 12. Music by him can also be heard in trailers for The Town, Lincoln and 2 Guns. His song Vengeance played a large part in the film The Equalizer and in trailers for Game of Thrones and 24: Live Another Day. In 2020 he made his debut as a director with the documentary BIRTH.

Hemsey shows how an independent musician without a record company can play a role in the world of the film trailer, a form of music in its own right that leans heavily on tension and build-up. His bombastic, dramatic style has been decisive for much of the music used in trailers.
artiest/zack-hemsey.listen: Listen to Mind Heist and notice how the tension slowly increases, with repeated motifs and more and more layers. Can you hear why it suits a trailer so well?

artiest/zakir-hussain.text: Zakir Hussain learned tabla from his father Alla Rakha, Ravi Shankar's regular accompanist. He played with the great soloists of Indian classical music, but also sought out other music: in 1975 the first album of Shakti appeared, his group with the guitarist John McLaughlin. Planet Drum, which he made with Mickey Hart, won the first Grammy for world music in 1992. His tabla sounded like a conversation with the soloist.
artiest/zakir-hussain.listen: Listen to Lotus Feet by Shakti: here the tabla does not play a strict rhythm, but soft, plucking patterns beneath the guitar and violin.

artiest/zangeres-zonder-naam.text:
The Zangeres Zonder Naam (the Singer Without a Name) was the stage pseudonym of Mary Servaes-Beij, born in Leiden in 1919. She was the eighth child in a working-class family and suffered from a broken hip from an early age. In Maastricht she sang in cafés. In 1957 she sang backing vocals on a demo that ended up with the producer Johnny Hoes. He heard a child's voice, turned out to have discovered a thirty-seven-year-old woman and gave her a record contract. He had no name for her remarkable voice, so he invented the artist name Zangeres Zonder Naam.

In 1959 her first gold single appeared, Ach vaderlief, toe drink niet meer. After that she had hits until the 1980s with, among others, De blinde soldaat, Mexico and Mandolinen in Nicosia. She recorded almost six hundred songs and was nicknamed the Queen of the Levenslied. The levenslied is the Dutch street song, full of sentimental stories about sorrow, mothers and soldiers, with accordion and orchestral accompaniment. In 1986 she performed at Paradiso, and her live record from that concert won an Edison in 1987.

She also sang protest songs. In 1977 she recorded Luister Anita, against Anita Bryant's anti-gay campaign, and performed at the concert Miami Nightmare. Writers such as Gerard Reve and Lucebert admired her, and so she also reached an audience of artists. She died in 1998.
artiest/zangeres-zonder-naam.listen: Listen to Ach vaderlief, toe drink niet meer and notice how her voice begins as a child's voice and how the story is told in the song. What feelings does the melody evoke?

artiest/zapp.text:
Zapp was an American funk band from Dayton, Ohio, built around the singer and multi-instrumentalist Roger Troutman and his brothers Larry, Lester and Terry. Roger began recording in the 1960s and formed Roger & The Human Body in 1976. In 1977 he took over the nickname Zapp from his brother Terry. Friends Bootsy and Phelps Collins, known from Parliament-Funkadelic, heard the band, and Bootsy invited Roger to the studio in Detroit. George Clinton helped get the demo of More Bounce to the Ounce to Warner Bros., which signed the group in 1979.

The self-titled debut was released in 1980. More Bounce to the Ounce reached number two on the American R&B chart. The second album, Zapp II (1982), went gold, and it included the number 1 single Dancefloor (Part I) on the R&B chart. Zapp III (1983), The New Zapp IV U (1985) and Zapp V (1989) followed, with diminishing success. In the 1990s Zapp came back via hip hop: Roger sang on the talk box on Tupac Shakur's California Love from 1995. In 1999 he was shot dead by his brother Larry, who then killed himself. The album Zapp VI: Back by Popular Demand was released in 2003.

The sound of Zapp is funk with electronics: bouncing bass, tight, drum-machine-like rhythms and the talk box, an effect in which you use a tube in your mouth to shape the sound of an instrument into speech. That gave the voice something robotic. The group was influential in electro-funk and gave West Coast hip hop and G-funk many samples. Ice Cube said that More Bounce to the Ounce introduced him to hip hop.
artiest/zapp.listen: Listen to More Bounce to the Ounce and notice the talk box: how the singing voice sounds like an electronic instrument. Listen, too, to the danceable, bouncing bass.

artiest/zawinul-syndicate.text:
The Zawinul Syndicate was a jazz fusion band founded in 1988 by the Austrian keyboard player Joe Zawinul, after his previous group Weather Report had developed into something else. It was a changing company of musicians from all kinds of countries. Zawinul chose the name Syndicate because, in his view, such a group is more like a family than just a band. The debut The Immigrants was released the same year, with, among others, Abraham Laboriel on bass, Cornell Rochester on drums and Scott Henderson on guitar.

Black Water (1989) and Lost Tribes (1992) followed, with Mike Baker on drums and Randy Bernsen on guitar. The live albums World Tour (1998) and Vienna Nights (2005) came later, as did 75th (2008), which won a Grammy. The musicians who played in it include Paco Sery, Manolo Badrena, Arto Tunçboyacıyan, Richard Bona, Victor Bailey, Karim Ziad and Aziz Sahmaoui. The group's last concert took place on 3 August 2007 in Güssing, six weeks before Zawinul's death. Afterwards some members continued under the shorter name The Syndicate.

The sound consists of a jazz groove with rhythms from all over the world, supplemented with vocals, percussion from Africa and Latin America and Zawinul's synthesizers. The band held on to the improvisation of jazz, but relied just as much on driving, swinging grooves. In this way it continued the line of Weather Report and became a model for world music within jazz.
artiest/zawinul-syndicate.listen: Listen to a track from The Immigrants and notice how Zawinul's synthesizer floats above a rhythmic groove. Try to pick apart the different rhythms of the bass, drums and percussion.

artiest/zbigniew-namys-owski.text: The alto saxophonist Zbigniew Namysłowski was born in Warsaw in 1939. He first played piano, cello and trombone before switching to the saxophone. With his quartet he recorded Lola in London in 1964, for Decca: one of the first Polish jazz records to be released in the West. In 1965 he played on Krzysztof Komeda's Astigmatic. Namysłowski wove Polish folk dances into his music, such as the oberek and the kujawiak, often in unusual metres of five or seven beats. You can hear that on Winobranie (1973) and Kujaviak Goes Funky (1975). He continued to perform well into old age and died in 2022.
artiest/zbigniew-namys-owski.listen: Count along: here the metre often does not have four beats, but five or seven.

artiest/zbigniew-preisner.text: Zbigniew Preisner was born in Bielsko-Biała and lives and works in Kraków. He taught himself to compose by writing out music from records; at university he studied history and philosophy. From Bez końca (1985) he worked with the director Krzysztof Kieślowski, including on the TV series Dekalog (1988), La double vie de Véronique (1991) and the trilogy Trois couleurs (1993–1994). Preisner invented a non-existent Dutch composer from the eighteenth century, Van den Budenmayer. His music plays a role in the stories, as a piece that characters sing or search for. Preisner's sound is simple and solemn: long choral lines, solo voice, strings, piano and oboe. In Bleu a choral work on a Greek text from the Bible is the musical centre of the film.
artiest/zbigniew-preisner.listen: Notice the austere, solemn choral and solo voices and how a single melody sounds like 'old music' within the story itself.

artiest/zbigniew-seifert.text:
Zbigniew Seifert was born in Kraków in 1946 and died in 1979, at the age of thirty-two, of cancer. He began as an alto saxophonist and was strongly influenced by John Coltrane. His real breakthrough came when he joined Tomasz Stańko's quintet in 1970 and focused on the jazz violin. After that he was regarded as one of the most important modern jazz violinists.

In 1973 he moved to Germany, where in 1974 and 1975 he played in Free Sound, Hans Koller's group. In 1976 he performed with John Lewis at the Montreux Jazz Festival, and later he recorded with the group Oregon. His albums include Kunstkopfindianer from 1974, Man of the Light from 1976 and Kilimanjaro from 1979. After his death more recordings appeared, such as Solo Violin.

In his hands the violin does not sound as it does in classical music but like a saxophone, with long, winding lines and a raw, intense tone. His early death made him known mainly among musicians and far less to the general public. His playing shows how the free and modal jazz of Coltrane could also sound on a string instrument.
artiest/zbigniew-seifert.listen: Listen to Man of the Light and notice how the violin moves freely, almost like a singing saxophone. Try to tell the long lines and the quick ornaments apart.

artiest/zdenek-liska.text:
Zdeněk Liška was a Czech composer who was born in 1922 in Smečno near Kladno, in central Bohemia. His father and grandfather were amateur musicians. As a child he learned accordion and violin, and in secondary school he wrote his first song. He studied composition and conducting at the Prague Conservatory and graduated in 1944. In 1945 he joined the Zlín Film Studios. There began a career in film music that would last until his death in 1983.

In the 1950s and 1960s Liška was the most sought-after film composer in Czechoslovakia. In the 1960s he wrote the music for about eight films a year, plus countless short films. He wrote the music for many titles of the Czechoslovak New Wave, including The Shop on Main Street, Marketa Lazarová, The Valley of the Bees, The Cremator and Ikarie XB-1. He also collaborated often with the animator Jan Švankmajer, including on Punch and Judy, The Flat and Jabberwocky, and wrote for Karel Zeman, Laterna Magika and travel documentaries. His main theme for the television series Thirty Cases of Major Zeman is still played by rock bands in the Czech Republic.

Liška was a pioneer of electronic music in film. He used unusual combinations of instruments and electronic and electro-acoustic techniques, and also experimented with pop music and rock, at a time when the film symphony was still the norm. He was known for his character sketches in music and for his humour. In this way he gave Czech film of the 1960s its own recognisable sound.
artiest/zdenek-liska.listen: Listen to the music of The Cremator or Marketa Lazarová and notice the unusual tone colours. Try to hear how an ordinary orchestra is blended with strange, electronic or processed sounds.

artiest/zeami.text:
Zeami Motokiyo, also called Kanze Motokiyo, lived from about 1363 to about 1443. He was a Japanese actor, playwright and thinker on theatre, and is regarded as the most important writer of Noh theatre. His father Kan'ami led a theatre company and saw early on that his son had talent. When the young shogun Ashikaga Yoshimitsu saw him perform, he took the actor under his wing. At court Zeami received a classical education in literature, poetry and philosophy, which was unusual for an actor. After his father's death in 1385 he took over the leadership of the company.

Zeami wrote an estimated fifty plays. Many of them draw their material from the Heike monogatari. Well-known titles include Atsumori, Takasago, Izutsu, Matsukaze and Yamanba. He combined folk dance, drama and music with classical poetry. He also wrote twenty-one treatises on the principles of Noh, including Fūshikaden. These are among the oldest writings on theatre in Japan, but they only became widely known in the twentieth century. After Yoshimitsu's death things became harder for him. In 1434 he was banished by the shogun Yoshinori to the island of Sado. After the shogun's death in 1441 he returned to the mainland.

Noh is a theatrical art in which slow dance, sung and spoken text, masks and a small ensemble of flute and drums come together. Zeami brought this art to its classical peak. His plays have been performed in Japan without interruption since they were written, and his ideas about beauty, silence and the flower of a performance still resonate in Japanese art.
artiest/zeami.listen: Listen to a recording of Noh and notice the singing of the chorus, the flute and the hand drums. Notice how long silence and tension are sustained before a sound follows.

artiest/zeami-motokiyo.text: Zeami Motokiyo appeared on stage as a child in the troupe of his father Kan'ami and received the protection of the shogun Ashikaga Yoshimitsu in 1374. He wrote plays that are still performed, such as Izutsu and Atsumori, and in his treatise Fūshikaden he explained how a performance builds tension according to jo-ha-kyū: slow, then faster, then fast. In 1434 he was banished to the island of Sado. His years of birth and death are approximate.
artiest/zeami-motokiyo.listen: No recordings exist from Zeami's time. Listen to Takasago, a Noh piece attributed to him, and hear the calls of the drummers between the beats.

artiest/zero-7.text:
Zero 7 is a British duo of Henry Binns and Sam Hardaker, formed in 1997. They studied sound engineering and worked in the 1990s at RAK Studios in London, where they made music for, among others, Pet Shop Boys, Young Disciples and Robert Plant. Their name came from a remix they made of Radiohead's Climbing Up the Walls, the Zero 7 Mix. They had chosen the name after a stay on the Honduran island of Utila, where a bar was called Cero Siete.

Their first EP appeared in 1999. The debut album Simple Things was released in 2001 and reached number twenty-eight in the British album chart, with singers such as Mozez, Sia and Sophie Barker. It was nominated for the Mercury Music Prize. When It Falls followed in 2004, with Tina Dico added, and The Garden in 2006, with José González. Yeah Ghost was released in 2009. After a quiet period In the Half Light appeared in 2024.

Zero 7 makes downtempo: calm, warm music with a soft beat, jazzy chords and electronic details. The two have sung little themselves and often chose a guest singer. In the early years of this century they therefore often ended up on lounge and chill-out compilations, and showed how pleasant electronic music could sound as background listening too.
artiest/zero-7.listen: Listen to Destiny and notice the calm beat and the soft vocals that seem almost to float over it. Can you hear which instruments hide beneath the electronics?

artiest/zhao-jiping.text:
Zhao Jiping is a Chinese composer, born in August 1945 in Pingliang in Gansu province and originally from Shaanxi. He studied at the Central Conservatory of Music in Beijing. He became known above all for his film music for directors of the so-called Fifth Generation, and in particular for Zhang Yimou. Later he became honorary chairman of the Chinese Musicians' Association.

His film music includes Yellow Earth, Red Sorghum, Raise the Red Lantern, The Story of Qiu Ju, 霸王别姬 (Farewell My Concubine), Red Firecracker, Green Firecracker, To Live, The Emperor and the Assassin and A Chinese Odyssey. He also wrote for the television series The Water Margin and Three Kingdoms. Much of this music has been released on album, such as Farewell My Concubine (1993), Raise the Red Lantern (1994) and The First Emperor (1998). In addition, The Magic Notes Of Zhao Jiping appeared in 2014.

Zhao Jiping's music is known for the way it links Chinese melodies and instruments from his own region to the image. In this way he contributed to the international success of Chinese cinema in the 1980s and 1990s. Anyone who knows Zhang Yimou's films also knows his sound: the music is so strongly bound up with those images that it is hard to imagine without the film. His work shows how film music can become part of a country's musical history.
artiest/zhao-jiping.listen: Listen to an excerpt from the film music for Raise the Red Lantern or Farewell My Concubine. Notice the Chinese instruments and how the music carries the mood of the image.

artiest/zia-fariduddin-dagar.text:
Zia Fariduddin Dagar was an Indian singer from the dhrupad tradition, the oldest surviving form of North Indian classical music. He was born in 1932 in Udaipur in Rajasthan, where his father Ziauddin Khan was court musician to the maharana. His father taught him dhrupad singing and veena. After his father's death he continued his studies with his elder brother, the veena player Zia Mohiuddin Dagar. Both belong to the Dagar family, a famous dynasty of dhrupad musicians.

From about 1980 he lived mainly in Austria, where he taught dhrupad at the Innsbruck conservatory, and also in France. His pupil, the filmmaker Mani Kaul, asked him to make the music for the film The Cloud Door (1994). He then returned to India, where he taught for 25 years at the Dhrupad Kendra in Bhopal. His pupils included the Gundecha Brothers, Uday Bhawalkar, Nirmalya Dey and Marianne Svasek. Later he lived in his brother's gurukul near Panvel, near Mumbai, and performed until shortly before his death in 2013. He received, among other honours, the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1994 and the Tansen Samman in 1993. Recordings can be heard on albums such as Le chant Dhrupad de Ustad Zia Fariduddin Dagar (1985) and Raag Malkauns: Bombay 1968, made together with his brother.

Dhrupad is a solemn, meditative form of singing. The singer builds up a raga slowly, first without rhythm and without text, accompanied by tanpura. Through his work as a singer and teacher, Zia Fariduddin Dagar helped keep this ancient art alive in India and Europe.
artiest/zia-fariduddin-dagar.listen: Listen to Raag Malkauns: Bombay 1968 and notice the slow beginning, the alap, in which the voice builds up the raga without rhythm. Try to hear how the note is first held for a long time before the movement increases.

artiest/zia-mohiuddin-dagar.text:
Zia Mohiuddin Dagar, Z. M. Dagar for short, was an Indian musician from the dhrupad tradition. He was born in 1929 in Udaipur in Rajasthan and belonged to the nineteenth generation of the Dagar family. His father Ziauddin Khan Dagar was court musician to the maharana. He learned singing and the rudra veena, an instrument on which singers practised their melodies and which traditionally was not played in public. He chose it as his main instrument nonetheless and gave his first recital at the age of sixteen.

After his father's death he adapted the instrument for solo playing. With the help of an instrument maker he enlarged the gourds and the hollow neck, so that the sound resonated for longer and the vocal techniques of dhrupad could be followed better. It became a larger, deeper instrument, which he played seated in the southern posture. In this way he contributed greatly to the revival of the rudra veena as a solo instrument. His time was hard: after Indian independence in 1947 the family lost the court as its patron. They lived in Mumbai and for twenty-five years barely made ends meet. In 1982 he founded the Dhrupad Gurukul near Panvel, a school where a few pupils live in with their teacher. Recordings include Raga Yaman (1991), Rudra Veena Recital (1974) and Raag Malkauns: Bombay 1968, which he made with his brother.

His playing was known for the slow development of a raga, usually with only a tanpura, and for the careful microtonal ornaments. He also taught in the West, including in Berkeley, at Wesleyan University and in Seattle. He died in 1990.
artiest/zia-mohiuddin-dagar.listen: Listen to Raga Yaman on the rudra veena and notice how slowly the raga unfolds. Hear how the low, resonant strings let each note ring on before the next one arrives.

artiest/ziryab.text: Ziryab was a singer and oud player at the court of Baghdad and came to Córdoba around 822, at the invitation of the emir Abd ar-Rahman II. The stories about him were largely written down centuries later, so his dates (born around 789, died around 857) and many anecdotes are uncertain. According to tradition he gave the oud a fifth pair of strings and founded a music school for men and women. For this reason he is regarded as the forefather of Andalusian music.
artiest/ziryab.listen: No music of Ziryab's own has survived. Listen to the Iraqi oud player Naseer Shamma, who dedicated an album to him: hear how the oud begins freely and without a fixed metre, like a taqsim.

artiest/zohar-fresco.text:
Zohar Fresco is an Israeli percussionist and composer, born in 1969, who specialises in the frame drum. He is known for a technique of his own on this instrument, in which he combines different styles. In the 1990s he played in Bustan Abraham, an Israeli world music band that existed from 1991 to 2003. With them he made albums such as Bustan Abraham (1992), Fanar (1997) with Zakir Hussain and Hariprasad Chaurasia, Hamsa and Ashra (2000). He also played in the Ziryab Trio, which made the album Mashreq Classics in 1997.

Since the beginning of this century he has been a member of the jazz trio of the Polish pianist Leszek Możdżer and the Swedish bassist Lars Danielsson. Together they made, among others, The Time (2005), Between Us and the Light (2006), Live (2007) and Polska (2013). He also played with the jazz drummer Hamid Drake, the violinist Taiseer Elias, the saxophonist Daniel Zamir and the oud player Ara Dinkjian, among others, and toured with the American composer Philip Glass. Later releases include Tof Miriam (2015) and Tarab (2018).

The frame drum is one of the oldest instruments in the world and occurs in music from the Middle East to Europe. Fresco uses it not only as rhythmic accompaniment but also as a melodic and sonorous instrument, with many tone colours from fingers, palm and rim. In this way he brings the rhythms of the Middle East into a jazz trio and shows that ancient percussion instruments have a place in contemporary music.
artiest/zohar-fresco.listen: Listen to Polska by the trio with Możdżer and Danielsson and notice the frame drum. Try to hear how Fresco makes both soft taps and deep strokes with his fingers and palm.

artiest/zoltan-kocsis.text:
Zoltán Kocsis was a Hungarian pianist, conductor and composer, born in 1952 in Budapest. He began music at the age of five and from 1963 studied at the Bartók Conservatory and later at the Franz Liszt Academy, where Pál Kadosa, Ferenc Rados and György Kurtág were his teachers. In 1970 he won the Hungarian Radio's Beethoven Competition and in 1971 he made his first tour of the United States. He received the Liszt Prize in 1973 and the Kossuth Prize in 1978.

Kocsis played with, among others, the Berliner Philharmoniker, the Chicago Symphony Orchestra, the New York Philharmonic and the Wiener Philharmoniker. He recorded Béla Bartók's complete solo works for piano and the works for piano and orchestra. In 1990 he won a Gramophone award for his recording of Debussy's Images and other piano works. In 1983 he founded the Budapest Festival Orchestra with Iván Fischer, and from 1987 he also led it as a conductor. From 1997 until his death in 2016 he was music director of the Hungarian National Philharmonic. He also wrote original works and arrangements of music by Wagner, Rachmaninoff, Bartók and Debussy, and in 2010 he completed the last act of Schoenberg's opera Moses und Aron.

According to Grove Music he had an impressive technique and a direct, strongly rhythmic style of playing that nevertheless never sounded mechanical. He felt at home with Bach, but also with contemporary music, and gave the first performances of work by Kurtág. With his playing of Bartók and with his orchestra he helped give the Hungarian classical tradition a new face.
artiest/zoltan-kocsis.listen: Listen to his recording of Debussy's Images and notice the tone colours he draws from the piano. Notice how softly and precisely the chords are struck.

artiest/zoot-sims.text:
Zoot Sims, born John Haley Sims in 1925 in Inglewood, California, was an American jazz saxophonist. He played mainly tenor saxophone, and later alto and soprano as well. His parents were vaudeville performers. He began on tenor at thirteen and took Lester Young, Ben Webster and Don Byas as his models. He got his nickname as a boy of fifteen in Kenny Baker's band, where the word Zoot was on the music stand he sat behind. He then played in the big bands of, among others, Benny Goodman, Artie Shaw, Stan Kenton and Buddy Rich.

He became known as one of the Four Brothers, the saxophone quartet in Woody Herman's big band. From 1954 to 1956 he toured with the sextet of his friend Gerry Mulligan, and in the early 1960s with Mulligan's Concert Jazz Band. With Al Cohn he led a group of his own for years. Albums from his long career include Zoot! (1956), Al and Zoot (1957), Jazz Mission to Moscow (1962), and from 1975 records for Pablo Records, such as Zoot Sims and the Gershwin Brothers and Basie & Zoot (1976). He also played a thirty-second solo on Phoebe Snow's Poetry Man (1974) and on Laura Nyro's Lonely Women. He died in New York in 1985.

Sims played with a loose, swinging tone, which combined the relaxed sound of Lester Young with the improvisational power of Charlie Parker. In his solos he stayed close to the melody, so that it remained recognisable. Colleagues regarded him as one of the strongest swingers. He showed that the soft, singing tenor tone of the swing era also had a place in modern jazz.
artiest/zoot-sims.listen: Listen to Phoebe Snow's Poetry Man and notice Zoot Sims's short saxophone solo. Notice how a few notes are enough for a loose, singing phrase.

genre/2-tone.text: Around 1969 the first skinheads adopted the ska and reggae of Jamaican migrants. In 1979 Jerry Dammers founded the label 2 Tone in Coventry, with deliberately mixed bands that played ska with the energy of punk: The Specials, The Selecter and The Beat. Madness also began on the label. Ghost Town (1981) is about cities emptying out because of unemployment.
genre/2-tone.listen: In Ghost Town, hear the slow ska rhythm on the offbeat, the minor chords and the horns that recall the Middle East.

genre/8-bit-en-chiptune.text: The first game consoles had no recorded music. A sound chip produced simple waveforms, and the composer had to program every note. Nintendo's NES had five channels: two square waves for melody and accompaniment, a triangle wave for the bass, a noise channel for percussion and a channel for short samples. For Super Mario Bros. (1985) Koji Kondo wrote melodies that suit running and jumping and can repeat endlessly. Hirokazu Tanaka gave Metroid (1986) a lonely, dark atmosphere. On the Sega Mega Drive, FM synthesis was heard. With it Yuzo Koshiro brought club and house music into the game in Streets of Rage (1991). Later a music scene of its own grew up around this sound: chiptune.
genre/8-bit-en-chiptune.listen: Count the layers: hear how melody, bass and rhythm each have a channel of their own, and how fast arpeggios suggest chords that the chip cannot play at once.
